We are seeking a highly technical Economist to join the OpenAI Economic Research team studying the real-world economic impacts of AI.
This role is designed for economists with up to 5 years of professional experience post-Ph.D. who are interested in using novel, large-scale datasets to study how AI is reshaping economic systems.

We are looking for candidates with deep expertise in at least one core domain relevant to AI’s economic impact, and an interest in contributing to a broader research agenda spanning labor markets, firm behavior, market dynamics, and macroeconomic change.

This is an individual contributor role where the candidate will organize and execute on their own data-oriented projects.
You will work at the intersection of economic research, data science, and public policy to produce rigorous empirical work that informs decision-makers across the public, industry, and government.
Research Areas of Interest
We are particularly interested in candidates with demonstrated expertise in one or more of the following areas:
Economic Measurement of AI Impact (e.g., adoption trajectories, labor market transitions, productivity growth, and forecasting/scenario modeling for AI-driven economic change)
Macroeconomic Implications of AI (e.g., productivity, technology diffusion, economic growth)
AI and the Labor Market (e.g., employment, wages, job search, task-level impacts, skill acquisition)
Applicants are not expected to have experience across all domains. We aim to build a team with complementary strengths across these areas.

Design and execute empirical research using large-scale observational or experimental data.
Apply causal inference and/or structural modeling techniques to study AI-driven economic change.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate research questions into testable frameworks and applicable takeaways across policy, product, and our organization.
Produce policy-relevant outputs, including academic papers, technical reports, and briefings.
Contribute to the development of new measurement approaches for AI’s economic impact.
Use AI across your responsibilities to scale your research impact.

· Draft, maintain, and iterate on Fraud & Scams policies governing Anthropic's products and APIs, with clarity for both model enforcement and human reviewers

· Conduct regular structured policy reviews to identify gaps, ambiguities, and coverage failures, and lead the process to close them

· Define and manage precision/recall tradeoffs in enforcement, working with data science teams to continuously tune classifiers and detection signals

· Build and maintain an effective feedback loop between threat intelligence, policy, and enforcement operations to ensure timely response to novel and evolving fraud threats

Technical & Cross-functional Collaboration

· Serve as the primary policy point of contact for ML and Engineering teams developing fraud detection classifiers, working to translate policy intent into technical artifacts and training signals

· Partner with Product, Engineering, and Data Science teams to optimize detection models, automated enforcement pipelines, and tooling for fraud-specific policy violations

· Collaborate with external researchers, law enforcement liaisons, and fraud SMEs to gather feedback on policy effectiveness and emerging risk areas

· Educate and align internal stakeholders — including Legal, Public Policy, and Go-to-Market teams — around Anthropic's fraud and scams policies and enforcement approach

This position is officially titled Economist. The working title is Senior Economist. As a Senior Economist, the selectee will serve as an authoritative expert in matters concerning economic impacts of Commission actions or proposed actions.

The Senior Economist will use a thorough knowledge of the economic literature and the methods used by other agencies, and other information to plan, carry out, or manage studies to improve the Directorate's analysis of the societal costs of injuries and benefits assessment.

The Senior Economist will plan, organize, and carry out major studies of the financial and economic impacts of product safety standards or other Commission regulatory, compliance, or litigation actions, including the effect on production and distribution costs, prices, employment, marketing, competition and industry structure, business practices, consumer behavior, financial conditions of firms and foreign trade.

The Senior Economist will be responsible for: Maintaining a broad understanding of benefits estimation methodologies in the economic literature. Maintaining and improving the Directorate's methods of estimating the societal cost of injuries and deaths for purposes of regulatory analysis.

Conducting regulatory and other analyses of product safety rules and other areas of major Commission importance. Developing the model and research methodology to be used in the studies, consulting with supervisors, other economists, and attorneys as necessary.

When appropriate, conducting special research and studies of high visibility for use in the preparation of reports. These efforts may include multiple regression analysis, design of surveys, or other theoretical and applied approaches to problem solving.

When required, preparing oral and written depositions and court testimony and serving as expert witness for the Commission on matters relating economic, statistical and financial analyses issues in litigation actions. When directed, serving as the representative to meetings, conferences, etc., which relate to the economists area of expertise.
